title: Carrageenan Air Pouch Protocol for Mice
author: Laura Ruiz Remolina
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j8dcrs6
materials: 3-	Day 6: Carrageenan Injection. We dissolve 1% Carrageenan (λ-Carrageenan Sigma-Aldrich) in 1X PBS. (eg 0.03g of carrageenan and 3ml of PBS). Carrageenan takes time to dissolve completely. We heat a bath at 80 ° C, give it vortex, and so on until it dissolves completely. Fresh carrageenan should be used. With the 30G needle we puncture 0.5 ml of carrageenan in the pouch while massaging the area. Once injected, massage for 30s.

steps.title: Inflate air pouch (Day 0)
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse, then inject 3 ml sterile air into the back to create the pouch.

substeps.instruction: Open O₂ bottle and set O₂ pressure between 0.5 and 1; set isoflurane flow to 4.
Place paper in the methacrylate anesthesia box, open the red stopcock, and direct O₂/isoflurane to the box.
Place the mouse under the nozzle, keep the nozzle stopcock open, and lower isoflurane pressure to 2 once the mouse is asleep.
Using a 10 ml syringe fitted with a 0.22 µm filter and a 30 G needle, infuse 3 ml sterile air into the mouse’s back.
Turn the needle while withdrawing to prevent air escape and form the pouch near the head so the mouse cannot bite it.

steps.title: Reinforce pouch (Day 3)
steps.instruction: Refill the existing air pouch with 3 ml sterile air using the same syringe/needle setup as on Day 0.

steps.title: Wash pouch with PBS (Day 7)
steps.instruction: At 24 h after carrageenan injection, wash the pouch with cold heparinized 1× PBS.

substeps.instruction: Label a 2 ml Eppendorf tube for each mouse.
Prepare a beaker of cold heparinized 1× PBS and keep it on ice.
Using a 21 G needle, inject 2 ml cold PBS into the pouch.
Massage the pouch for 30 s without removing the needle, taking care not to damage the mouse.
Slowly withdraw the needle and syringe, applying minimal pressure.
